harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1, node2, node3 as a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (mariadb-server-galera 10.5.29, galera 26.4.22 from RHEL 9 AppStream). Bootstrapped node1 via galera_new_cluster, joined node2 and node3 via SST (mariabackup). Had to fix a SELinux AVC denial (mysqld_t self connectto on unix_stream_socket, required for the mariabackup SST donor/joiner) by loading a small local policy module (mysqld_sst.pp) on all three nodes. Opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567(tcp+udp)/4568 on all nodes. Verified writes from any of the three members replicate synchronously to the other two. Demonstrated availability during a member outage: stopped node3, cluster stayed Primary with 2/3 quorum and accepted writes; on node3 restart it auto-resynced via IST and picked up the write made while it was down. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id + healthy Synced/Primary status + data on each node, restarted node1, node2, then node3 one at a time via `systemctl reboot` (backgrounded so the ack returned first), polled each until reachable again, confirmed changed boot_id, and confirmed each rejoined as Synced/Primary with cluster_size 3 and correct data after every restart, only proceeding to the next node once full health/quorum was restored. Final cross-node write/read check after all restarts confirms consistent replication. Root and SST credentials were generated on node1 with openssl and distributed to node2/node3 over cluster SSH; not included in this report (the SST password did appear in one earlier debug `cat` command's tool output, but was not reused or logged further).
actions_performed: Inspected OS (RHEL 9.8) and root/sudo access on all 3 nodes
Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, mariadb-backup, galera from AppStream on all 3 nodes
Configured /etc/hosts with cluster host mappings on all 3 nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567(tcp,udp)/4568 on all 3 nodes
Confirmed SELinux mysqld_port_t already covered Galera ports
Set up cluster SSH keypair for inter-node file transfer
Generated SST auth password and MariaDB root password on node1 via openssl and securely copied to node2/node3 over SSH
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf wsrep configuration (cluster address, node name/address, mariabackup SST) on all 3 nodes, correcting the galera provider .so path
Bootstrapped Galera cluster on node1 with galera_new_cluster; enabled mariadb service
Created sstuser account and set root password on node1

Diagnosed SST failure (mariadb-backup socket connect EACCES) as a missing SELinux allow rule (mysqld_t self connectto unix_stream_socket) via audit.log; built and loaded a local policy module (mysqld_sst.pp) on all 3 nodes
Started/joined node2 and node3 to the cluster via SST; enabled mariadb on both
Verified 3-node cluster: wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary on all nodes
Verified write-from-any-node replication with a test table (writes from node1, node2, node3 all visible everywhere)
Stopped node3 to test availability under member outage; confirmed 2-node quorum stayed Primary and accepted a write
Restarted node3; confirmed automatic resync (IST) picked up the write made during its outage

Executed mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id + healthy status/data baseline, sequentially rebooted node1, node2, node3 (one at a time, waiting for full cluster health before the next), polled each until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and confirmed mariadb auto-started/rejoined as Synced/Primary with correct data after each restart
Performed final post-restart write/read check from node3 confirming replication to node1 and node2

evidence.requirement: Three-member Galera cluster configured; writes through any member visible on the others
evidence.summary: All 3 nodes report wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced/Primary; inserts made on node1, node2, and node3 each appear on all other nodes' SELECTs.

evidence.requirement: Root cause / fix for SST failures (SELinux)
evidence.summary: AVC denial for mysqld_t self connectto unix_stream_socket found in audit.log; local policy module built and loaded on all 3 nodes to permit the Galera SST donor/joiner socket connection.

evidence.requirement: Node2 and node3 successfully joined the cluster via SST
evidence.summary: node2 started active and reported wsrep_cluster_size=2/Synced after SST; node3 started active on first attempt (post-fix) and reported wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced/Primary.

evidence.requirement: Database stays available when one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: node3 stopped; node1 (2/3 nodes) still reports cluster_status=Primary, wsrep_ready=ON, and accepts an INSERT that immediately appears on node2.

evidence.requirement: Unavailable member resynchronizes automatically when it returns
evidence.summary: node3 restarted, cluster_size returned to 3/Synced, and the row written while node3 was down is present on node3 without manual intervention (automatic IST).

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4999270d.../Synced/Primary + data captured; reboot acked before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id 175700d9... (changed); mariadb auto-started/enabled and rejoined as cluster_size=3/Synced/Primary with all rows intact.

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bef0e5ec.../Synced/Primary + data captured; reboot acked; post-reboot boot_id 8f59c869... (changed); mariadb active/enabled and rejoined as cluster_size=3/Synced/Primary with data intact.

evidence.requirement: Node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 31949c21.../Synced/Primary + data captured; reboot acked; post-reboot boot_id 1371e686... (changed); mariadb active/enabled and rejoined as cluster_size=3/Synced/Primary with all incoming_addresses present and data intact.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart full-cluster write/replication check across all members
evidence.summary: After all three restarts, a write on node3 (id=6) is immediately visible on both node1 and node2, confirming full bidirectional replication survives the restart sequence.
